rules: IsApproved is ALWAYS false on pulled/test queue items — never submit a real auth from a test run.
Never persist PHI (member names, DOBs, IDs, phones) — redact to placeholders in filenames/docs.
Never commit credentials — bearer/passwords stay in local config, read at runtime.

The UiPath 'Authorization Dev Clone' folder (434039) is NOT a BE sandbox: every BackendApi call (AuthScreenshot, confirmSubmit, ...) is real there exactly as in 'Authorization' (231517), aimed at whatever serverURL the queue item names. Only IsApproved=false stops a real submission, and only a pre-prod serverURL keeps BE writes off prod — this MCP's queue-item guard enforces both.

This MCP never writes to prod: queue-item POSTs/deletes and job starts/stops are pre_prod-only (UiPath dev clone 434039, Apex 'Authorization Test'; schema-enforced as a JSON-schema const AND asserted in the domain function) and it never repins releases, deploys, or creates Processes/queues; it never touches Apex credentials, assets or Action Center.

Every posted queue item (either orchestrator) passes the test-safety guard: IsApproved forced false, serverURL/queueUrl pinned to the configured pre-prod values (fails closed when unconfigured), <TO-FILL> placeholders rejected.

delete_queue_item is fetch-first and refuses any item whose status is not New; stop_job is fetch-first and refuses a job already in a terminal state (UiPath Successful/Faulted/Stopped; Apex also lost/timed_out).

Apex prod and test folders share one deployment and one login, so the folder is the only boundary: the Apex client always sends X-Folder-Id, refuses any non-GET request unless env=pre_prod (before any network call), refuses a write when the pre_prod and prod folders resolve to the same id, never takes a folder override on writes, and never auto-retries a write. stop_job additionally refuses a job outside the pre_prod folder; delete_queue_item refuses a queue missing from the pre_prod folder's listing.

Copilot BE writes target pre-prod only: every write engine (create_preprod_order, submit_preprod_order, delete_preprod_order, apply_settings_sync) refuses prod-tagged AND untagged clients (fails closed). create_preprod_order always stops at forReview and never submits; only submit_preprod_order submits, and only with explicit user authorization.

Every Copilot tool requires an explicit env (prod | pre_prod) and profile — nothing defaults either (list_clinics takes env only; orchestrator tools take env but no profile). All Copilot BE logins go through one auth chokepoint; sessions are cached and single-flighted so the support account's login budget is not burned.

Settings sync is plan/apply and additive: plan_settings_sync is read-only; apply_settings_sync re-plans server-side, executes only the selected actionIds or an explicit all:true (exactly one required), copies prod-only settings into pre-prod, and never overwrites or deletes. Env-specific references are remapped by name; anything unmatched is dropped with a warning.

get_job_artifacts writes only under ~/.cache/copilot-mcp/artifacts/ (directory mode 0700), never inside a repo. Treat everything downloaded (job.log adapter lines, result_payload, screenshots, trace.zip) as PHI: never commit, paste or summarize its contents.

Read caches are persistent but conservative: only terminal-and-settled jobs (5 min after end; 15 min for Apex cancelled/lost/timed_out) are ever stored, only after a live read in the same call confirms it, and no cache ever feeds a write guard or a fetch-first refusal. They live on disk under the cache dir (dirs 0700, files 0600) and hold PHI at rest — never commit or paste them; copilot.sessionCache:false keeps everything in memory. Pass refresh:true to get_job / get_job_logs / build_faulted_job_issue / get_job_artifacts to bypass a cached result.
stdout is the JSON-RPC channel: the server never prints anything else to it; diagnostics go to stderr.
